Welcome to Ballard
Welcome to multi-award-winning Ballard School, a place where pupils belong, thrive and achieve.
Ballard is a joyful, ambitious and welcoming school where education is truly transformational. Confident, curious and kind, Ballard pupils flourish across our exceptional campus, in classrooms, on the sports fields and on stage. Financially secure and proudly independent as a charitable trust, we are free to focus every resource on delivering an outstanding education and nurturing every child.
Set within beautiful surroundings between the New Forest and the Solent, our forward-thinking, values-led approach has earned national recognition, winning this year’s coveted Independent School of the Year Award (South), two years after being named Co-Educational School of the Year (2024/25). Recognised by The Telegraph as one of its Best Value Private Schools, Ballard has won the Global 100 Award for Best Education Management (UK) and the ISA Award for Fine Art & Design, while retaining Eco-Schools Green Flag with Distinction and School Games Gold status. Ballard has further strengthened its reputation by reaching the ISA finals for both Sport and Sustainability.
Describing Ballard as “a joyful, friendly sanctuary in the New Forest”, The Good Schools Guide highlights our beautiful grounds and resources, extraordinary sense of community and impressive results, noting that creativity is nurtured through exceptional arts provision that pupils throw themselves into.
These honours and accolades reflect a vibrant, inclusive community where learning is purposeful and pupils feel known, supported and inspired.
Explore our website to discover the ‘Ballard Effect’ for yourself: the learning, the opportunities, the sense of belonging, and the joy of a school community that continues to move from strength to strength.

The School’s Vision Statement
Ballard is a place where pupils feel known, supported and inspired. Rooted in strong values and excellent teaching, we help every child achieve their personal best be that in the classroom, on the stage, on the pitch and beyond.
Our broad curriculum and rich co‑curricular life build confidence, character and curiosity, preparing young people for their next steps with kindness, ambition and a strong sense of community. This nurturing, relational approach, often described by families as The Ballard Effect, is what makes us distinctive.
Aims
The aims of the school may be summarised as follows:
We celebrate strengths and support challenges, helping each pupil grow in a community where they feel genuinely known, understood and encouraged.
We stretch, support and inspire pupils so they can achieve their personal best.
Relationships matter: we promote kindness, respect, open communication and trust.
4. Develop character and purpose
We help pupils build character by developing confidence, resilience and a clear sense of right and wrong.
5. Build confidence for the future
We help pupils develop independence, adaptability and confidence, qualities that will serve them well in an ever‑changing world.
6. Celebrate individuality
We champion diversity, talent and the unique contributions each pupil brings.
Above all we believe character is shaped by challenge as much as success. At Ballard, our response is always the same: clarity, kindness and care.
The School Charter (the Ballard BEEs)

« Avoir une autre langue, c’est posséder une deuxième âme » To have a second language is to have a second soul Charlemagne, King of the Franks, 768-814
The French Department aims to equip pupils with a solid foundation of knowledge and communication skills to encourage them to flourish with courage, curiosity and compassion as independent global citizens. Through learning French, we want to open a world of new possibilities and opportunities for our pupils, deepen their understanding of their own culture and those of others, and to foster a lifelong love of language learning.
Our specialist teachers work with our pupils from Year 1 all the way to Year 11. Our impressive GCSE examination results are a testament to the quality of teaching and learning taking place throughout a pupil’s French experience at Ballard. We bring French to life through a number of fun events and experiences: cooking and tasting traditional food, a virtual exchange with our partner school in Vendée, themed days at school, trips to France, and of course our after-school clubs which offer opportunities to have fun with the language, raise attainment or practise conversation and debating skills in la langue de Molière.
Pre-Prep
French is taught from Year 1 by our Head of French, accompanied by our lovely French bear, Camembear. Together they cover a wide range of cross-curricular topics in French using songs, rhymes, games, activities and stories.
Each week our star pupil is given the opportunity to go home with one of Camembear’s cousins and our young learners enjoy practising new words and phrases with them.
Lower Prep
Pupils continue to learn through games, stories and role plays and follow the adventure of an English family moving to France, where they make new friends and learn about life in a different country. The emphasis is placed on speaking as much as possible with a light-touch introduction to key grammatical concepts which support children’s literacy and provide a strong grounding for their move to the upper section of the school.
Upper Prep
Pupils in Year 6 and above have their own French digital notebooks and access to a number of engaging online learning platforms. As the language taught becomes more complex, pupils continue to progress as confident language learners and delve deeper into how to manipulate vocabulary and structures. They finish their time in this section of the school with a visit to Normandy and are able to put their language skills to the test.
Senior
On entering the Senior school, pupils focus their attention on expanding the breadth of their vocabulary and grammatical knowledge. Our objective remains the same: to develop students’ French language skills and to give them the tools and knowledge to communicate in a variety of contexts with confidence. Alongside rigorous preparation for the AQA French GCSE, the language is brought to life through cultural events, language learning competitions and our link to like-minded students from our partner school in France.
Co-curricular
GCSE French (Years 10 & 11).
Normandy Trip – Year 8
An immersive, 5 day, action-packed trip which includes the discovery of Le Mont St Michel and a visit to the tapisserie de Bayeux, buying your own picnic at the market and learning to make bread, as well as many other exciting activities while staying in our very own château.

Drama is more than performance – it’s a powerful tool for developing:
Pupils at Ballard benefit from specialist teachers for Expressive Arts and Drama throughout their journey at Ballard, as well benefiting from our outstanding facilities, which include a 200-seater Performing Arts Centre.
Drama is also enriched by our wealth of co-curricular opportunities, including LAMDA exams and drama clubs.
Pre-Prep
In Pre-Prep, Drama is often integrated into play-based learning and literacy. A firm favourite with pupils is building our own shadow puppet theatres where we act out our stories.
We focus on role-play, storytelling, movement, and expression. This helps develop skills in:
Listening and responding
Speaking clearly and confidently
Exploring emotions and social situations
Using imagination and creativity
Lower Prep
Pupils in Lower Prep begin to explore structured Drama activities and basic performance techniques through their Expressive Arts lessons.
We focus on character creation, improvisation, and group work and aim to develop skills in:
Pupils also have the opportunity to participate in annual Drama performances.
Vocal projection and body language
Teamwork and collaboration
Understanding narrative and structure
Responding to feedback
Upper Prep
Drama in Upper Prep becomes more formalised, with opportunities for performance and analysis.
We focus on script work, stagecraft, and dramatic techniques and aim to develop skills in:
Pupils also have the opportunity to participate in annual Drama performances.
Interpretation of text and character
Use of space, props, and costumes
Reflective practice and peer critique
Exploring social and historical contexts
Senior
Drama is offered as a GCSE subject and becomes a rigorous academic and creative discipline.
Senior pupils focus on performance, theory, and evaluation, where we aim to develop skills in:
Advanced acting and directing
Script analysis and dramaturgy
Understanding theatre history and genres
Preparing for public performance and exams
Co-curricular
Top Hat Theatre Drama (Years 7 & 8), GCSE Performing Arts Support (Years 10 & 11).

Pupils in Year 6 and above have their own French digital notebooks and access to a number of engaging online learning platforms. As the language taught becomes more complex, pupils continue to progress as confident language learners and delve deeper into how to manipulate vocabulary and structures. They finish their time in this section of the school with a visit to Normandy and are able to put their language skills to the test.
Senior
On entering the Senior school, pupils focus their attention on expanding the breadth of their vocabulary and grammatical knowledge. Our objective remains the same: to develop students’ French language skills and to give them the tools and knowledge to communicate in a variety of contexts with confidence. Alongside rigorous preparation for the AQA French GCSE, the language is brought to life through cultural events, language learning competitions and our link to like-minded students from our partner school in France.
Co-curricular
GCSE French (Years 10 & 11).
Normandy Trip – Year 8
An immersive, 5 day, action-packed trip which includes the discovery of Le Mont St Michel and a visit to the tapisserie de Bayeux, buying your own picnic at the market and learning to make bread, as well as many other exciting activities while staying in our very own château.

Pre-Prep

Listening and responding
Speaking clearly and confidently
Exploring emotions and social situations
Using imagination and creativity
Lower Prep
Pupils in Lower Prep begin to explore structured Drama activities and basic performance techniques through their Expressive Arts lessons.
We focus on character creation, improvisation, and group work and aim to develop skills in:
Pupils also have the opportunity to participate in annual Drama performances.

Teamwork and collaboration

Upper Prep
Drama in Upper Prep becomes more formalised, with opportunities for performance and analysis.
We focus on script work, stagecraft, and dramatic techniques and aim to develop skills in:
Pupils also have the opportunity to participate in annual Drama performances.

Exploring social and historical contexts

“To achieve great things, two things are needed; a plan and not quite enough time.”
Leonard Bernstein
Creating, performing, listening and appraising, the Ballard Music Department is a hub of creative energy, where pupils and staff enjoy keeping music live and relevant. A varied ensemble programme, pupil bands, studio work, recitals, concerts, trips, festivals, gigs, school shows, sound and lighting, Specialist Visiting Music Teachers and 1:1 lessons, the Music Mentor Programme – there is all to play for! From Mozart to Metallica and Shostakovich to Singing in the Rain, good music is good music no matter the genre. Create, Perform, Go beyond…
We are incredibly proud that in an era when music education is being squeezed nationally, it continues to thrive at Ballard.
The Music Department is staffed by enthusiastic and energetic teachers, committed to making music fun and fulfilling for all; they have a range of specialist skills from the classical and commercial world in both instrumental and vocal work. Music is part of the curriculum from KG – Year 11, with a track record of 100% A*- C at GCSE and 100% Pass to Distinction Grades 1-8 for Music Exams (ABRSM/Trinty). Highlights from our performance calendar include our Carol Service at Christchurch Priory, Informal Christmas and Summer concerts, the Classical Concert at Beaulieu Abbey Church, European Tour, and Musical Productions for all ages.
Pre-Prep
Pre-Prep music at Ballard is all about fostering a sense of enjoyment and achievement, building confidence, co-ordination and collaborative skills through a variety of fun activities (singing, playing instruments, listening, discussing and reacting to music and basic notation).
All children participate in performances, including the annual Nativity and Summer Showcase and have the opportunity of instrumental lessons (age dependent).
Lower Prep
Lower Prep pupils receive weekly music lessons from our specialist teachers in our well-equipped music building and iMac Studio.
Pupils study composers (classical-contemporary) and their music, composition skills (iMac Studio), musical notation, and a range of fun, practical activities to increase musicianship skills (class ensembles, band work, vocal groups).
Pupils also enjoy an Expressive Arts programme, working across music, dance and drama to prepare for a range of performances including an annual musical production.
Upper Prep
Upper Prep pupils receive weekly music lessons from our specialist teachers in our well-equipped music building and iMac Studio.
Pupils study composers (classical-contemporary) and their music, composition skills (iMac Studio), musical notation, and a range of fun, practical activities to increase musicianship skills (class ensembles, band work, vocal groups).
Pupils in Year 6 also enjoy an Expressive Arts programme, working across music, dance and drama to prepare for a range of performances including an annual musical production.
Senior
Year 9 pupils receive weekly music lessons from our specialist teachers in our well-equipped music building and iMac Studio.
Pupils study composers (classical-contemporary) and their music, composition skills (iMac Studio), musical notation, and a range of fun, practical activities to increase musicianship skills (class ensembles, band work, vocal groups).
Year 10 and Year 11 GCSE pupils have a wide range of opportunities to help prepare them for the next stage of their music education and the wider world of the music industry, whether it be contemporary or classical, or progressing from GCSE music to study music at 6th Form.
Co-Curricular
String Ensemble (Years 1 to 11), Junior Choir (Years 3 to 5), Harp Ensemble (Years 3 to 5), PA Junior Band (Years 3 to 5), Handbells (Years 6 to 9), Show Chorus (Years 6 to 11), Chamber Ensemble (Years 7 to 11), Showband (Years 8 to 11), Chamber Choir (Years 6 to 8), Drum Ensemble (Years 6 to 11), Guitar Ensemble (Years 6 to 11), Orchestra (Years 6 to 11), Chamber Choir Upper Voices (Years 8 to 11), Junior Show Band (Years 6 to 8), Chamber Choir (Years 9 to 11), Showband (Years 8 to 11).

pageCache.pageTitle: Ballard School Music Department – Spring Recital Series Review – Ballard School
pageCache.text:
Our amazing Spring Music Recitals were absolutely superb.
It’s another example of all the wonderful opportunities here @ Ballard.
Our Head of Music, Mr P said
“Over the course of two weeks, the Music Department presented a remarkable series of four recitals, each one a celebration of dedication, musical growth, and the joy of performance. The PAC was filled at every event, with a wonderfully supportive audience of parents, friends, family members, and grandparents, whose enthusiasm added real warmth to the occasion.
Across the series, there were an impressive eighty three performances, showcasing a wide range of ages from Years 1 to 11, instruments, and musical styles. Every pupil approached their performance with professionalism, musicality, and admirable composure. Whether they were stepping onto the concert platform for the very first time or building on previous recital experience, each performer contributed to an atmosphere of encouragement, achievement, and a genuine love for music making.
A heartfelt thank you goes to our dedicated Visiting Music Teachers, whose careful preparation, commitment, and support were evident in every performance. Their presence at the recitals and their ongoing encouragement play a vital role in nurturing the Ballard pupils’ confidence and musical development.
Holding this programme of recitals in the Spring Term remains an important part of musical life at Ballard. Not only does it provide valuable preparation for ABRSM exams at the end of term, but it also offers pupils the essential experience of performing a solo in the PAC in a supportive environment where they can practise and refine the skills that reach far beyond music itself. Confidence, organisation, presentation, teamwork, preparation, and consistent practice all come to life on the concert platform, helping Ballard’s young musicians grow into poised, capable individuals.
Congratulations to every performer on a wonderful fortnight of music making!”
You can see some of the amazing performances here.
